    BABLYTICSSIGNAL AMONG THE STACKS

    Bablytics — the Guide

    Fifteen readers. One ranked list every morning. A court every evening that grades the graders.

    A local, single-user research app. Each weekday thirteen graders, a Skeptic and an Executive read the market's library — options flow, headlines, disclosures, technicals, cycles — and sign a Top 20 of ten option leads and ten stock leads with a memo and house rules; after the close the Evening Court scores every call against the tape. Nothing it produces is a recommendation, and nothing it does places a trade.

    Download Get the reports by email Read the guide Meet the board

    The rhythm

    A trading day, as the board lives it

    Every time below is US Eastern, Monday to Friday, and every one of them is a scheduler job you can also run by hand. The weekend has its own pair of sessions. How a Day Runs walks through each stop.

    What's inside

    What the app does

    Thirteen mechanisms, each with its own page, and a mailing list for the reports. Every one runs in mock mode with no API key, so you can see the whole machine before you pay for a single model call.

    The Morning Briefing

    7:00 ET. Collectors build ~40 candidates; thirteen seats grade every one for the mandate you set — day trade, swing, long-term or a mix; the Skeptic rebuts; the Executive signs ten option leads and ten stock leads that fit it, with entry, live price, stop, target, a time horizon (swing · ≈5 sessions, and why), a read-across (betas, peers, "if this moves +1%…") and the day's house rules.

    Morning Briefing

    The Pre-Open Check

    9:15 ET. The whole committee re-reads the briefing against futures, pre-market prints, an open-interest conversion audit of yesterday's flow, analyst moves and the 8:30 prints — confirmed move, pump fake or undecided.

    Pre-Open Check

    The Midday Check-In

    12:30 ET. Every seat reads its own open Paper League positions at the midday mark and files one hold-or-close per position; closes are applied to the paper ledger.

    Midday Check-In

    The Evening Court

    19:00 ET. The day is scored against the close, the Pyramid re-forms, and all fifteen seats write where they were on base, off base, and the lesson — then the court trains the model population and reports what it did.

    Evening Court

    Reviews & Horizons

    Saturday 8:00 the week in review; Sunday 17:00 the week ahead; month and year editions on the period's edges. Includes your own scorecard from the trades you marked as taken.

    Reviews & Horizons

    The Pulse

    Every half hour of the session, five numpy actor-critic models vote — enter, add, hold, trim or exit — on your book, blended with the board's standing views and capped by house caution rules. Model opinion; nothing executes.

    The Pulse

    The Bailiff

    Reads the board's written invalidations, turns them into typed triggers, and enforces them in the record — the board's book and the Paper League — on the right basis: close, settle or intraday. Dry-run by default.

    The Bailiff

    The Paper League

    Fifteen autonomous paper books at $100,000 each — the thirteen graders, the Skeptic and The Bot, which trades the Executive's signed book. Which philosophy actually makes money on paper?

    Paper League

    The Fund

    One synthetic paper book that takes every lead the board grades 60 or better and holds it on that lead's own stop, target and horizon. A small transformer decides what fraction of the portfolio belongs in the book; a tax lens can veto a trim whose after-tax edge is not worth realizing. Paper money, nothing executes, tax figures are estimates.

    The Fund

    The Spotlight

    Every lead graded 60 or better — the same line the Fund admits on — gets a full strategy profile: the dated catalyst, what the options market is pricing against what the name actually does, structures priced off the real chain, and the nine conditions (intraday · swing · long-term × conservative · moderate · aggressive), with an honest "no position" wherever that is the answer.

    The Spotlight

    The Learning Loops

    Journal lessons feed the next morning's prompts; dossiers accumulate per seat; a small neural net learns which grades predict 5-day returns; the Pulse population evolves nightly behind a held-out gate.

    Learning Loops

    The Evidence Locker

    Drop your own PDFs, notes, spreadsheets, screenshots and voice memos on the dashboard; the extracted text and your note ride every board prompt as USER EVIDENCE, for the morning briefing and the evening court, and the seats must cite a document when it moves a grade. Files stay on your disk.

    Evidence Locker

    The Desk

    A dashboard you can rearrange, Charts Pro with thirty studies, a positions book with CSV upload and a log-a-trade form, a Schwab link that stages orders and never submits one without your click, news, the Library and the Archive.

    Dashboard & workspace

    The reports, by email

    No app needed: put your name on the list and Sean sends the Morning Briefing PDF each trading day, the Evening Court and the weekend Week in Review / Week Ahead — by hand, after each session. Research reports from an AI boardroom, never advice; name and email only; leave any time.

    Get the reports by email

    The seats

    The board: fifteen seats

    Thirteen seats grade every candidate from their own philosophy, the Skeptic attacks whatever survives with every grade in hand, and the Executive chairs — weighing each seat by its track record and the Pyramid. Four seats are inspired by the public philosophies of real people; they paraphrase published ideas and are not the people themselves. Full profiles, lineages and recent lessons are on The Board.

    🪑

    The Executive

    Chair of the Board — weighs every grade against its owner's record and signs the Top 20.

    🔎

    The Skeptic

    Devil's Advocate — attacks crowding, stale catalysts, liquidity traps and wishful thinking.

    📡

    Flow

    Options Flow Analyst — volume over open interest, skew, and fake footprints.

    🗡️

    Dagger

    Quant / Statistics — z-scores, regime, base rates; allergic to narratives.

    🏰

    The Chartist

    Castle-in-the-Air Technician — the exact levels the crowd and the bots are watching.

    🪟

    The Glazier

    Gap-Fill Statistician — which windows get glassed, at what odds, by when.

    🎯

    Sam

    Trading Discipline (after Sam Parikh) — expect zero, buy less, demand 3×, never counter-trend.

    🧓

    The Oracle

    Value & Quality (after Warren Buffett) — moats, owner earnings, margin of safety.

    📚

    Graham

    Value Discipline (after Benjamin Graham) — investment versus speculation, said out loud.

    🦢

    The Black Swan

    Risk Philosopher (after Nassim Taleb) — convexity, fragility hunting, ruin first.

    🎡

    The Croupier

    House-Edge Analyst (after “Hedging the Wheel”) — where is the edge, or eat the vig.

    🦅

    The Watchdog

    Government Trades Monitor — congressional disclosures, read cynically.

    🗞️

    Domestic Desk

    US News Correspondent — the Fed, the prints, earnings, Washington.

    🌍

    Foreign Desk

    Global News Correspondent — geopolitics, foreign central banks, commodities, supply chains.

    🕰️

    The Timekeeper

    Cycle Analyst — frequency decomposition of the index plus posted Curry-cycle forecasts.

    Read this

    Research tool — not financial advice

    Nothing Bablytics produces is a recommendation to buy or sell anything.

    Grades, memos, leans, exit zones and predictions are model output — frequently wrong, never personalized, and not reviewed by any licensed professional. The app executes no trades on its own: the Pulse and the Bailiff have no execution path, the Paper League is paper, and the optional Schwab link stages orders that go nowhere until you click submit on each one, behind a confirmation. Four personas are inspired by the public philosophies of real people (Sam Parikh, Warren Buffett, Benjamin Graham, Nassim Taleb); they paraphrase published ideas for personal research and are not affiliated with or endorsed by them. Options can expire worthless. Read the full statement on Not Financial Advice.
